anomalies.observed: On sheet 1 (POWER TRAIN) the board's AZ1117-3.3 LDO U2 has its VO pin connected to the global +3V3 net, AND the ESP32-C6-DevKit's on-board 5V→3.3V regulator M1B has its 3V3 pin also connected to the same global +3V3 net (M1B 5V0 is fed from +5V, so its internal LDO is active). Two independent 3.3 V linear-regulator outputs are therefore merged onto one rail.
anomalies.expected: The specification's power tree (§3) makes U2 the sole source of the +3V3 rail ("U2 ... VO feeds +3V3, which powers the I2C pull-ups, isolator primary sides, and TMC2209 logic") and powers the DevKit only from its 5V0 pin; it never routes the DevKit's 3V3 header pin onto the board +3V3 net. Standard practice also forbids paralleling two LDO outputs (back-feed / current fight).

evidence.quote: Sheet 1 POWER TRAIN: U2 'AZ1117-3.3' VO → +3V3 arrow; M1B 'ESP32-C6-DEVKIT' 5V0 → +5V and 3V3 → +3V3 arrow (same +3V3 global label).
§3: 'U2 AZ1117-3.3 LDO: +5V → +3V3 ... I2C pull-ups ... Primary side of U3/U4 ... TMC2209 logic'; DevKit is listed only as 'Powers ESP32-C6 DevKit (5V0 pin)'.

anomalies.impact: The +3V3 rail is driven by two regulators at once. Whichever has the slightly higher set-point sources the load while the other is reverse-currented into its output; this can cause regulation instability, reverse-bias stress on one LDO, and an unintended 3.3 V sourcing path not present in the reference design.

parsed.summary: Most of the drawing matches the specification (power tree, ADM3260 pH/EC isolation, TMC2209 drivers, float interlocks, DNP environmental sensors, and the LiDAR left as an unpopulated header are all consistent with the documented design and its known limitations). The one deviation I can support from the drawing is that the DevKit's on-board 3.3 V LDO output (M1B.3V3) is tied to the same +3V3 net that U2 regulates, paralleling two LDO sources that the specification's power tree keeps separate.
